separation_note: A mechanism change here is a change to executable behaviour inside this unit's owned subtree, already tested. Changes proposed for shared PO-03 paths are not applied by this unit and are recorded as unbound proposals in strategy-proposals.json, because workstreams/po03/tools/** and workstreams/po03/control/** are read-only to this attempt.

changes.title: Recovery scanner added as an executable event-stream control
changes.before: The commission requires a recovery scanner. The repository contained an append-only ledger, an outbox, a materialised recovery-state.json and a document-level validator, but no executable that derives current state from the event stream. Recovery state was maintained by the controller in parallel with the ledger rather than reconstructed from it.
changes.after: recovery_scan.py reconstructs current Obzio state for every task from the ledger alone, enforces the commission's refusal rules at the event layer, classifies each unit into a recovery disposition, and emits an idempotent replay directive per unit.
changes.why_the_event_layer_matters: The seeded validator sees one already-written result document and cannot detect a unit whose result was committed but never ingested, because no document is produced for a lost callback. That failure is only visible in the event stream.
changes.recurrence_test: run_recurrence.py, 151 pinned checks, rerun from a fresh no-hardlink clone

changes.title: Attempt identity normalised across three naming conventions
changes.discovered_by: Executing the first scanner build against the live ledger rather than against fixtures.
changes.before: Keying attempts on attempt_id alone, falling back to the idempotency-key suffix, split one logical attempt into two whenever the live ledger named it both ways. This produced 55 spurious ILLEGAL_TRANSITION_REFUSED defects on a ledger that is in fact clean, and left 55 of 508 events unapplied.
changes.after: attempt_id, the trailing segment of the idempotency key, and inheritance from the task's live attempt all normalise to one task-scoped key. All 508 live events apply and integrity is CLEAN.
changes.lesson: A recovery scanner validated only against fixtures its own author generated will encode the author's naming assumptions. Running against the live stream before writing the fixtures is what exposed this.

changes.title: False-completion guard placed above lifecycle legality
changes.before: COMPLETED was refused only when it violated the transition table, so a COMPLETED event arriving at a structurally legal position with no durable commit behind it would have been admitted. The summary also reported no false completion when the guard had in fact fired, because a refused event leaves completed false.
changes.after: A COMPLETED assertion is refused whenever the attempt holds no verified durable result commit, whatever its lifecycle position and whatever the actor. The report separates false_completion_admitted, which must always be empty, from false_completion_refused, which records the guard firing so the controller can still investigate.

changes.title: Duplicate redelivery no longer misreported as storage reordering
changes.before: The file-order check compared every line's event_seq, so an at-least-once transport re-appending an earlier event late in the file raised a spurious FILE_ORDER_NOT_SEQ_ORDER defect and turned integrity DEFECTIVE. A correctly functioning retry path therefore looked like disk corruption.
changes.after: The check considers only the first occurrence of each event_id, so legitimate redelivery is silent while genuine reordering is still reported. fx-06 is CLEAN and fx-14 remains DEFECTIVE.

changes.title: Scan survives a task whose every event is refused
changes.discovered_by: Adversarial test with an invalid fence token on a task's only event.
changes.before: The scan raised ValueError: max() iterable argument is empty. A single malformed event could crash the recovery scanner, which is the exact circumstance in which recovery is needed.
changes.after: Such tasks are named in unreconstructable_tasks and the scan completes. A task is never silently dropped: either it appears in tasks with a reconstruction, or it appears in unreconstructable_tasks with its refusals recorded as findings.

changes.title: Calendar validation added to instant parsing
changes.discovered_by: Adversarial test asserting that 2026-13-01T00:00:00Z is unparseable.
changes.before: The regular expression accepted any two-digit month and day, so month 13 or day 32 produced a plausible epoch value. A malformed lease_expires_at could therefore silently shift an orphan decision.
changes.after: Month, day with leap-year handling, hour, minute and second are range-checked, and an out-of-range instant returns None so a lease with an invalid expiry is treated as having no parseable expiry rather than a fabricated one.

changes.title: Producer self-acceptance diagnosed before the generic actor-prefix rule
changes.before: The generic unauthorized-reviewer check ran first, so a producer accepting its own result was reported as UNAUTHORIZED_REVIEW_ACTOR and the more specific PRODUCER_SELF_ACCEPTANCE branch was unreachable. The refusal was correct; the diagnosis was wrong, which matters because the two faults call for different controller responses.
changes.after: Self-acceptance is checked against the attempt's recorded producer actors first, so the specific fault is named. A reviewer that did not produce the attempt is still accepted normally.

changes.title: Fenced attempt with no successor no longer reported as handed over
changes.before: Any FENCED or SUPERSEDED_BEFORE_DISPATCH attempt was classified as NONE_SUCCESSOR_CARRIES_WORK, which asserts a successor exists. For a fenced attempt with no successor recorded this silently retires live work with no recovery action, which is a result-loss path.
changes.after: The successor claim is made only when successor_attempt_id is present. Otherwise the unit is ATTEMPT_FENCED_NO_SUCCESSOR with REDISPATCH_UNDER_NEW_FENCE.
